title: Grammar: Linking Words — Contrast, Concession, and Addition
grammarTip:
Дискурсивные маркеры (Discourse markers / Linking words) структурируют текст:

ДОБАВЛЕНИЕ: furthermore · in addition · moreover · besides · what is more
КОНТРАСТ: however · nevertheless · on the other hand · in contrast · yet
ПРИЧИНА: because · since · as · due to · owing to
РЕЗУЛЬТАТ: therefore · consequently · as a result · thus · hence
ПРИМЕР: for example · for instance · such as · namely · to illustrate
ВЫВОД: in conclusion · to sum up · overall · in summary · to conclude

⚠️ Используй маркеры осмысленно — не механически!
"Furthermore" должен добавлять действительно важную информацию.
"However" должен вводить реальный контраст.

grammarTable.subject: CONTRAST
grammarTable.verb: however, whereas, while, on the other hand, in contrast
grammarTable.example: "The novel is brilliantly written. However, its plot is weak."

grammarTable.subject: CONCESSION
grammarTable.verb: although, even though, despite, in spite of, nevertheless
grammarTable.short: acknowledging one side while arguing the other
grammarTable.example: "Although the film is flawed, it remains emotionally powerful."

grammarTable.subject: ADDITION
grammarTable.verb: furthermore, moreover, in addition, besides, not only…but also
grammarTable.example: "The acting is strong. Furthermore, the cinematography is exceptional."

grammarTable.subject: CAUSE
grammarTable.verb: because, since, as, owing to, due to, as a result of
grammarTable.example: "The film succeeded owing to its unconventional structure."

grammarTable.subject: EFFECT
grammarTable.verb: therefore, consequently, as a result, thus, hence
grammarTable.example: "The ending was ambiguous; consequently, audiences were divided."

grammarTable.subject: EXAMPLE
grammarTable.verb: for example, for instance, such as, in particular, namely
grammarTable.example: "Several critics praised specific scenes; for instance, the opening sequence."

rows.form: However: sentence start or mid-sentence, with comma
rows.example: "However, the film fails to develop its themes." / "The film, however, fails…"

rows.form: Whereas / While: mid-sentence, joining two clauses
rows.example: "The novel is tragic, whereas the film adaptation is comic."

rows.form: On the other hand: introduces the opposing point
rows.example: "The cast is excellent. On the other hand, the script is weak."

rows.form: In contrast: comparing to what was just said
rows.example: "Dickens wrote long, complex sentences. In contrast, Hemingway used short, direct ones."

rows.form: Although / Even though + subject + verb
rows.example: "Although the ending is ambiguous, it feels emotionally satisfying."

rows.form: Despite / In spite of + noun or gerund (-ing)
rows.example: "Despite its slow pace, the film is compelling." / "In spite of being flawed, it works."

rows.form: Nevertheless / Nonetheless: sentence start, acknowledging concession
rows.example: "The film has weaknesses. Nevertheless, it is worth watching."

rows.form: Even so / Even then: similar to nevertheless
rows.example: "The script was poor. Even so, the performances saved the film."

rows.form: Furthermore / Moreover: adds a stronger, supporting point
rows.example: "The cinematography is stunning. Furthermore, the score is unforgettable."

rows.form: In addition / Additionally: adds information
rows.example: "The film explores identity. In addition, it raises questions about memory."

rows.form: Not only…but also: emphasises both points equally
rows.example: "The film not only challenges its audience but also rewards them."

rows.form: Besides: adds a different kind of point (often informal)
rows.example: "The acting is strong. Besides, the story is genuinely original."

rows.form: ❌ Despite the film was slow, I enjoyed it.
rows.example: ✅ Despite the slow pace, I enjoyed it. (despite + noun/gerund, NOT + clause)

rows.form: ❌ Although of its flaws, the film succeeds.
rows.example: ✅ Despite its flaws, the film succeeds. (although + clause; despite + noun)

rows.form: ❌ The film is good, however the ending is weak.
rows.example: ✅ The film is good. However, the ending is weak. (however needs a new sentence or semicolon)

rows.form: ❌ Furthermore is the acting impressive.
rows.example: ✅ Furthermore, the acting is impressive. (normal word order after furthermore)

grammarExtra.title: Choosing the Right Linker for Academic Writing

rows.form: To introduce a contrasting point: however, whereas, on the other hand
rows.example: Preferred in formal essays and reviews.

rows.form: To acknowledge and counter: although, despite, nevertheless
rows.example: Essential for balanced critical writing.

rows.form: To strengthen with evidence: furthermore, moreover, in addition
rows.example: Build your argument progressively.

rows.form: To show cause-effect: therefore, consequently, as a result
rows.example: Analyse the impact of artistic choices.

exercises.text: "The film has a weak script. ___, the performances are outstanding."
"___ its slow pace, the novel is deeply rewarding."
"The director's previous film was dark and bleak. ___, this new one is surprisingly optimistic." (contrast)
exercises.hint: "In contrast" = comparing to the opposite of what was just stated

exercises.text: "Despite ___ the main award, the film received mixed reviews."
"The film explores grief beautifully. ___, it raises important questions about memory." (addition)

opts: Although of its flaws, the film succeeds.
Despite the film was flawed, it succeeds.
Although the film is flawed, it succeeds.
Despite that the film is flawed, it succeeds.
exercises.correct: Although the film is flawed, it succeeds.

exercises.instruction: Complete with "however" in the correct position.
exercises.text: "The screenplay is intelligent. ___, the dialogue often feels stilted." (start of second sentence)
exercises.hint: "However" at the start of a new sentence with a comma after it

exercises.instruction: Choose the most formal addition linker.
exercises.text: "The novel challenges colonial assumptions. ___, it reclaims indigenous narrative traditions."
exercises.hint: "Moreover" = formal; adds a stronger or more significant point

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct concession linker.
exercises.text: "The reviews were negative. ___, the film became a cult classic."
exercises.hint: "Nevertheless" = despite what was just said, the opposite happened

exercises.instruction: Which is a correct concession structure?
opts: Although its complexity, the film succeeds.
Despite the film is complex, it succeeds.
In spite of its complexity, the film succeeds.
Nonetheless its complexity, the film succeeds.
exercises.correct: In spite of its complexity, the film succeeds.
exercises.hint: "In spite of + noun" = concession; same as "despite"

exercises.text: "The film ___ tells a compelling story ___ raises profound moral questions."
exercises.hint: "Not only… but also" = emphasises both elements equally

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct contrast linker for comparing two things.
exercises.text: "The novel is character-driven, ___ the film adaptation focuses entirely on plot."
exercises.hint: "Whereas" = direct comparison of two contrasting things within one sentence

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct addition linker.
exercises.text: "The novel won the Booker Prize. ___, it was adapted into an acclaimed film." (adds a further achievement)

opts: The film is brilliant however it has some flaws.
The film is brilliant. However it has some flaws.
The film is brilliant. However, it has some flaws.
However the film is brilliant, it has some flaws.
exercises.correct: The film is brilliant. However, it has some flaws.
exercises.hint: "However" starts a new sentence followed by a comma

exercises.text: "___ the film is long, it never feels slow." / "___ its length, the film never feels slow."

exercises.instruction: Which linker introduces a contrast within the same sentence?
exercises.text: "The film is technically innovative, ___ its narrative is fairly conventional."
exercises.hint: "Whereas" mid-sentence: X is one way, whereas Y is another

questions.text: "___ being critically praised, the novel sold poorly on publication." (concession + noun/gerund)
"The acting is superb. ___, the script leaves much to be desired." (contrast)
"___ the film has some weaknesses, it remains one of the most important of the decade." (concession clause)
"The novel explores themes of identity. ___, it offers a powerful critique of colonial history." (addition)
questions.hint: "Moreover" = adds a further, significant supporting point

questions.text: "The film received negative reviews on release. ___, it has since become a cult classic." (unexpected positive result)
questions.hint: "Nevertheless" = despite negative outcome, the positive happened

questions.text: "Despite the film was slow, I enjoyed it" is grammatically correct.
"The novel ___ explores grief ___ offers a meditation on memory." (equal emphasis on both)
questions.hint: "Not only… but also" = equal emphasis on two points

questions.text: "Dickens used long sentences, ___ Hemingway preferred short, direct ones."
questions.hint: "Whereas" in a single sentence = direct comparison of two contrasting things

questions.text: "The novel won multiple awards. ___ ___ being awarded, it sold very few copies initially." (contrast — use "in spite of")
"The director's use of silence is striking. ___, the use of colour is equally effective." (addition)
questions.hint: "Furthermore" = adding a further, related supporting point

questions.text: "The film failed commercially. ___, it had a lasting influence on independent cinema." (unexpected positive despite negative)
questions.hint: "Nevertheless/Even so" = despite the failure, something positive happened

opts: The novel is brilliant, however it has flaws.
The novel is brilliant; however, it has flaws.
The novel is brilliant; however it has flaws.
The novel is brilliant however, it has flaws.
questions.correct: The novel is brilliant; however, it has flaws.
questions.hint: "However" after a semicolon and before a comma is standard punctuation
